metadata.title: We: The Nameless — Radical Contents
metadata.scope: Genesis–Kings only: the nine conventional books Gen Exo Lev Num Dtr Jos Jud Sam Kng
metadata.reference_system: Common English / KJV-style chapter and verse numbers; check against Hebrew anchors before implementation.
metadata.interpretation: The segmentation, English headings, and character-to-passage mappings are editorial proposals, not inherited Chinese biblical titles or claims about authorial divisions.
metadata.source_file_role: Authoritative supplied 104-unit inventory; the source Markdown and earlier radical notes provide rationale and preferences.
metadata.repeat_policy: Repeat a sign when its core meaning recurs; use stable section IDs rather than signs as unique identifiers.
metadata.validation_scope: The 100 units form exact consecutive unions of the 104 supplied core units. Validation proves preservation of the supplied partition, not an independent verse-by-verse audit of the manuscript’s absent Hebrew chapter includes.
metadata.count_definition: Count only books[].sections[]; distinct characters are the exact Unicode character values in those sections. Book emblems, lexical glosses, historical change records, and the separately archived coda are excluded.
metadata.book_emblem_policy: Keep 元 出 示 屯 申 土 士 王 主 unchanged. A glyph may occur at both hierarchy levels; it does not create an additional microbook or an additional microbook-vocabulary entry.
metadata.source_precedence: The latest Radicalized pair and the user’s explicit retention of 屯 govern current choices. Radicals 1 and Radicals 2 are historical rationale/candidate notes, not replacements for the latest inventory.
metadata.coda_policy: The 11 original Ezra–Nehemiah–Esther sections are preserved separately in Radicalized-coda.archive.json and are not part of the 100.
metadata.unique_character_target_note: 70 is the selected soft target. Reaching 40 would require substantially more substitutions and loss of specificity; no 40-sign variant is represented as completed.
metadata.tex_integration_status: A TeX support include, static contents, stable-ID markers, placement manifest, and integration instructions are supplied. Markers have not been inserted into the unavailable chapter files; English-to-Hebrew anchor mapping remains required.

books.name: Genesis

sections.title: Heaven and Earth
sections.rationale: The ordered world: light, divisions, living things, humanity, and rest.

sections.title: Humanity
sections.rationale: Earth becomes a person; companionship, desire, knowledge, work, and expulsion follow.

sections.title: Bloodlines
sections.rationale: Brothers, murder, descendants, and multiplying violence: blood as kinship and bloodshed.

sections.title: The Flood
sections.rationale: The household carried through destruction; renewed life, covenant, and another family rupture.

sections.title: The Scattering
sections.rationale: Peoples and languages divide; branching genealogies narrow toward one family.

sections.title: Go
sections.rationale: Terah’s migration, Abram’s departure, Egypt, separation from Lot, and the rescue expedition.

sections.title: The Cut
sections.rationale: Covenant, disputed offspring, renamed ancestors, and circumcision: promise written into divided flesh.

sections.title: Strangers
sections.rationale: Abraham’s visitors and Lot’s guests; hospitality, threatened households, destruction, and survival.

sections.title: The Son
sections.rationale: The threatened mother, the long-awaited child, the expelled child, and the endangered heir.

sections.title: Succession
sections.rationale: Sarah’s burial, Rebekah’s arrival, Abraham’s death, and the disposition of his descendants.

sections.title: Exchange
sections.rationale: Birthright, blessing, brides, wages, and flocks change hands. Jacob substitutes himself for the elder, then encounters substitutions and altered bargains in Laban’s household.

internal_transitions.title: Exchange in Laban’s household
internal_transitions.note: This former microbook boundary remains an internal editorial transition, not a separate counted unit.

sections.title: Homeward
sections.rationale: Return, wrestling, reconciliation, new names, bereavements, and the two brothers’ separate futures.

sections.title: Clothing
sections.rationale: Joseph’s robe, Tamar’s veil, an accusation-cloak, and royal dress: identities and fortunes change hands.

sections.title: Recognition
sections.rationale: The brothers are tested; Judah offers himself; concealment gives way to reunion.

sections.title: Grain
sections.rationale: A household migrates for food; hunger transfers Egypt’s property and labor to Pharaoh.

sections.title: Bones
sections.rationale: Final blessings, inheritances, burials, and the demand that Joseph’s remains eventually leave Egypt.

books.emblem_role: conventional-book header; excluded from microbook and microbook-vocabulary counts

books.name: Exodus

sections.title: Forced Work
sections.rationale: A population becomes a labor force; children are threatened, and Moses grows up and flees.

sections.title: The Name
sections.rationale: The cry is heard; Moses is commissioned; the divine name becomes a claim against Pharaoh.

sections.title: The Blows
sections.rationale: The contest of signs, the first nine plagues, and the announcement of the final blow.

sections.title: The Threshold
sections.rationale: Passover, marked doorways, death of the firstborn, departure, and its permanent observances.

sections.title: The Crossing
sections.rationale: The sea escape and its victory song form one completed movement.

sections.title: The Road
sections.rationale: Water, food, attack, and delegated judgment: learning to survive outside Egypt.

sections.title: The Mountain Covenant
sections.rationale: The Sinai encounter, commandments, case laws, public assent, covenant blood, and ascent form one movement from arrival to ratification.

internal_transitions.title: The covenant’s terms and ratification
internal_transitions.note: This former microbook boundary remains an internal editorial transition, not a separate counted unit.

sections.title: The Pattern
sections.rationale: The sanctuary, its furnishings, priestly service, workmanship, and Sabbath are prescribed.

sections.title: The Calf
sections.rationale: An image, a broken covenant, intercession, and renewed tablets.

sections.title: Willing Work
sections.rationale: Gifts and skilled work produce the sanctuary; the presence fills what the people have made.

books.emblem_role: conventional-book header; excluded from microbook and microbook-vocabulary counts

books.name: Leviticus

sections.title: Offerings
sections.rationale: The altar economy: burnt offerings, grain, shared meals, purification, restitution, and priestly portions.

sections.title: Ordination
sections.rationale: The priests are established; service begins; unauthorized fire kills Aaron’s sons.

sections.title: Distinctions
sections.rationale: Edible and inedible, clean and unclean: animals, childbirth, skin, houses, and bodily flows.

sections.title: Removal
sections.rationale: The sanctuary is cleansed and wrongdoing is carried away by the dispatched goat.

sections.title: Life Together
sections.rationale: Blood and life, sexual boundaries, neighbors, holiness, and penalties for violating the social order.

sections.title: Sacred Access
sections.rationale: Who may serve, what may be offered, and who may eat sacred food.

sections.title: Sacred Time
sections.rationale: Festivals, perpetual light, and recurring bread: the sanctuary’s calendar and continuities.

sections.title: The Name on Trial
sections.rationale: Blasphemy, testimony, punishment, and the relation between injury and redress.

sections.title: The Land and Its Rest
sections.rationale: Sabbath years, Jubilee, redemption, and limits on ownership lead into abundance, devastation, exile, and the land recovering its neglected rest.

internal_transitions.title: The covenant’s consequences
internal_transitions.note: This former microbook boundary remains an internal editorial transition, not a separate counted unit.

sections.title: Valuations
sections.rationale: Vows, dedicated property, redemption, and tithes: what an obligation is worth.

books.emblem_role: conventional-book header; excluded from microbook and microbook-vocabulary counts

books.name: Numbers

sections.title: The Muster
sections.rationale: The first census, tribal arrangement, Levite counts, and assigned responsibilities.

sections.title: The Center
sections.rationale: The camp is ordered around sacred presence: purity, vows, blessing, gifts, service, cloud, and signals.

sections.title: Mouths
sections.rationale: The march begins; hunger, complaint, prophecy, and challenges to Moses turn on mouths and speech.

sections.title: The Scouts
sections.rationale: The land is seen, described, feared, and refused; one generation loses its future there.

sections.title: The Staff
sections.rationale: Rules, rebellion, Aaron’s budding staff, priestly entitlements, and purification establish contested authority.

sections.title: The Last March
sections.rationale: Leaders die; water fails; routes close; snakes, wells, and battles mark the approach to Moab.

sections.title: The Oracle
sections.rationale: Balaam is hired to curse, but his mouth cannot deliver the outcome his patron purchases.

sections.title: The Spear
sections.rationale: Baal-peor, the plague, and Phinehas’s violent enforcement of the boundary.

sections.title: The Recount
sections.rationale: A replacement generation is counted; daughters claim inheritance; Joshua is appointed.

sections.title: Obligations
sections.rationale: Recurring offerings and binding or annulled vows: what must be kept.

sections.title: Spoils and Shares
sections.rationale: The Midian war and its division of captives and goods; the eastern tribes negotiate their share.

sections.title: The Inheritance
sections.rationale: The itinerary becomes a claim to land: borders, towns, refuge, and rules keeping inheritances within tribes.

books.emblem_role: conventional-book header; excluded from microbook and microbook-vocabulary counts

books.name: Deuteronomy

sections.title: Retelling
sections.rationale: The journey, failures, victories, exclusions, and obligations are stated again.

sections.title: Allegiance
sections.rationale: The commandments reach inward: love, memory, humility, loyalty, and the danger of forgetting.

sections.title: One Center
sections.rationale: One chosen place organizes worship, belonging, shared provision, release, and the pilgrimage festivals.

sections.title: Authority
sections.rationale: Judges, courts, kings, priests, and prophets: who may decide, rule, or speak.

sections.title: Bloodguilt
sections.rationale: Refuge, witnesses, warfare, and the unaccounted-for corpse: responsibility for bloodshed.

sections.title: Neighbors
sections.rationale: The law enters households, fields, debts, disputes, vulnerable lives, and everyday dealings.

sections.title: Firstfruits
sections.rationale: A farmer gives produce and recites how a dispossessed people received its land.

sections.title: Choose Life
sections.rationale: Mutual declaration, covenant sanctions, exile, return, and the choice between life and death.

sections.title: The Witness
sections.rationale: Leadership passes on; law and song are entrusted to the people as testimony for the future.

sections.title: The Limit
sections.rationale: Moses’s final blessing, forbidden crossing, last view, and death.

books.emblem_role: conventional-book header; excluded from microbook and microbook-vocabulary counts

books.name: Joshua

sections.title: Entry
sections.rationale: Commission, reconnaissance, Jordan crossing, memorial, circumcision, and Passover complete the entrance.

sections.title: Conquest
sections.rationale: The armed encounter introduces the campaigns, their failures and victories, and the list of defeated kings.

sections.title: Allotment
sections.rationale: The land is divided into inheritances, borders, towns, and places of refuge.

sections.title: Belonging
sections.rationale: An altar almost makes the tribes enemies; they negotiate what it means to belong together.
changes: reused an existing character; boundary and title unchanged
sections.character_choice_note: Shared belonging is retained under the existing sign for joining and union; the threatened rupture ends in recognized membership rather than war.

sections.title: Witness
sections.rationale: Farewell, covenant, the witnessing stone, and the burial notices establish an obligation to remember.

books.emblem_role: conventional-book header; excluded from microbook and microbook-vocabulary counts

books.name: Judges

sections.title: Unfinished
sections.rationale: Incomplete possession, surviving peoples, a dying generation, and recurrent disloyalty set the conditions.

sections.title: The Left Hand
sections.rationale: The opening deliverers, dominated by Ehud’s concealed, left-handed reversal of power.

sections.title: Women
sections.rationale: Deborah and Jael overturn the expected distribution of authority and victory; prose and song stay together.

sections.title: The Few
sections.rationale: Gideon’s reduced force wins; vengeance, wealth, and quasi-royal power complicate the deliverance.

sections.title: The Trees
sections.rationale: The fable of trees seeking a king frames Abimelech’s kingship and its destruction; minor judges close the unit.

sections.title: Fatal Words
sections.rationale: Jephthah’s negotiations, vow, and the shibboleth test make speech a matter of life and death.

sections.title: Strength
sections.rationale: Samson’s force, appetite, vulnerability, captivity, and last act.

sections.title: Portable Gods
sections.rationale: An image and a priest change owners; Dan takes a shrine and a city.

sections.title: War Within
sections.rationale: The concubine’s abuse and death lead to intertribal war and the abduction of women to preserve Benjamin.

books.emblem_role: conventional-book header; excluded from microbook and microbook-vocabulary counts

books.name: Samuel

sections.title: Hearing
sections.rationale: Hannah’s prayer, Eli’s household, and the child who learns to distinguish a call.

sections.title: The Captive God
sections.rationale: The Ark is captured, humiliates its captors, returns, and is followed by renewed national allegiance.

sections.title: The First King
sections.rationale: The request for a king, Saul’s selection and establishment, his wars, and his rejection form the first kingship’s founding and failure. David’s rise begins the next unit.

internal_transitions.title: The king tested and rejected
internal_transitions.note: This former microbook boundary remains an internal editorial transition, not a separate counted unit.

sections.title: The Rival Rises
sections.rationale: David is anointed, fights, enters the royal household, and becomes the target of the king’s fear.

sections.title: The Fugitive
sections.rationale: David gathers followers, moves among refuges, negotiates alliances, and twice spares Saul.
changes: reused an existing character; boundary and title unchanged
sections.character_choice_note: The fugitive’s journeys reuse the established movement sign. The title and rationale preserve the distinction between chosen migration and forced flight.

sections.title: The Fallen
sections.rationale: David serves abroad; Saul seeks the dead and joins them; lament completes the fall.

sections.title: Union
sections.rationale: Rival royal houses fight until all the tribes acknowledge David.

sections.title: The House
sections.rationale: Capital, palace, Ark, dynasty, dependents, and conquests: the house of David is established.

sections.title: Taking
sections.rationale: David takes Bathsheba and arranges Uriah’s death; Nathan answers with the story of a stolen lamb.

sections.title: The Children
sections.rationale: Tamar, Amnon, and Absalom expose the violence within the royal household.

sections.title: Revolt
sections.rationale: Absalom’s rebellion, David’s flight and return, and Sheba’s secession undo the image of secure union.

sections.title: The Reckoning
sections.rationale: Famine, warriors, songs, last words, and a deadly census form the reign’s retrospective record.

books.emblem_role: conventional-book header; excluded from microbook and microbook-vocabulary counts

books.name: Kings

sections.title: Succession
sections.rationale: Solomon gains the throne; David dies; rivals and dangerous survivors are removed.

sections.title: The Listening Heart
sections.rationale: Solomon’s judgment and administration establish the promise of wise government.

sections.title: The House Built
sections.rationale: Temple, palace, furnishings, dedication, and the joining of sacred house with royal house.

sections.title: Gold
sections.rationale: Wealth, work, trade, prestige, marriages, and divided allegiance expose the costs of magnificence.

sections.title: Division
sections.rationale: The kingdom splits; rival shrines and unstable dynasties give the division enduring form.

sections.title: Fire and Voice
sections.rationale: Elijah’s drought, provision, Carmel contest, and the voice beyond the fire.

sections.title: The Word Against Kings
sections.rationale: War, Naboth’s vineyard, disputed prophecy, and the deaths of Ahab and Ahaziah.
changes: reused an existing character; boundary and title unchanged
sections.character_choice_note: Prophetic mouths, disputed testimony, and lethal speech reuse the sign already used in Numbers and Judges. The mouths of prophets are explicit in 1 Kings 22:22–23.

sections.title: The Mantle
sections.rationale: Elijah’s mantle passes to Elisha; inherited prophetic authority acts through provision, healing, war, and royal succession.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.rationale: The dynastic setup leads to Jehu’s killing campaign against the Omrides and the Baal establishment.

sections.title: Restoration
sections.rationale: A surviving royal child is installed; the temple is repaired.

sections.title: Israel Lost
sections.rationale: Dynastic attrition, wars, and foreign pressure culminate in the northern kingdom’s removal.

sections.title: Holding Out
sections.rationale: Hezekiah’s reforms, the Assyrian siege, recovery, and the ominous visit from Babylon.

sections.title: Undoing
sections.rationale: Manasseh and Amon reverse the preceding reform and deepen the announced judgment.

sections.title: The Book Found
sections.rationale: A discovered text judges the kingdom; Josiah reorganizes worship and then dies.

sections.title: Judah Lost
sections.rationale: Dependent kings, conquest, destroyed city and temple, deportation, assassination, and flight to Egypt.

sections.title: Survival
sections.rationale: Jehoiachin leaves prison and receives a place and food at a foreign king’s table: survival, not restored sovereignty.

merges.title: Exchange
merges.rationale: Birthright, blessing, brides, wages, and flocks change hands. Jacob substitutes himself for the elder, then encounters substitutions and altered bargains in Laban’s household.
merges.editorial_reason: The exchanges at home and the exchanges abroad form a single arc: the deceiver becomes the deceived. The homeward movement remains a separate microbook.

merges.title: The Mountain Covenant
merges.rationale: The Sinai encounter, commandments, case laws, public assent, covenant blood, and ascent form one movement from arrival to ratification.
merges.editorial_reason: The mountain encounter and the covenant’s terms belong to one enacted agreement; the sanctuary pattern still begins separately at Exodus 25:1.

merges.title: The Land and Its Rest
merges.rationale: Sabbath years, Jubilee, redemption, and limits on ownership lead into abundance, devastation, exile, and the land recovering its neglected rest.
merges.editorial_reason: Leviticus 25 commands the land’s rest; 26:34–35 describes its rest during the inhabitants’ exile. Land, release, obligation, and consequence remain together.

merges.title: The First King
merges.rationale: The request for a king, Saul’s selection and establishment, his wars, and his rejection form the first kingship’s founding and failure. David’s rise begins the next unit.
merges.editorial_reason: The institution is requested, established, tested, and disowned before the narrative turns to David’s anointing at 1 Samuel 16:1. Saul’s later death and its lament remain separate.
